$comment: ★★★ LABELS INSIDE AN INLINE-ASM TEMPLATE, AND THE TEMPLATE TEXT FORMS gcc AND clang EXPAND (P68 round 8, D-ASM-LABELS-INSIDE-A-TEMPLATE-AND-NUMERIC-LOCAL-LABELS-REFUSED and D-ASM-TEMPLATE-FORMS-A-REFERENCE-EXPANDS-REFUSED). A label a template defines is a block of the STATEMENT's own body, so nothing the register allocator writes can land inside it; `1b` / `1f` resolve by position through the ONE resolver a `.s` asks too; `%=` is one number per asm INSTANCE. The shapes: a loop on `1:`; `1:` defined twice in one template, each `1b` taking the nearest; a loop on `again%=` in TWO statements of one function; `1f` over one instruction both ways; a `9f` written after one `9:` that must reach the NEXT one; and the forms — x86 `mov{l} {%1, %0|%0, %1}` (the AT&T alternative), `%;%+%^%!` in front of a real instruction (gcc prints nothing for each), `%{ %} %| %* %= %~` in a comment; aarch64 `%{ %} %=` in a comment. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23 at -O0 and -O2: gcc 13.3.0 runs this file to 42 on x86_64 and clang 18.1.3 runs it to 42 on aarch64 (qemu); clang x86_64 refuses only gcc's punctuation forms and gcc aarch64 only `%{ %}` — the union accepts every form, and with the forms reduced to `%=` all four run it to 42. DSS refused every template label at the parser and every form at the semantic tier. ★ RED-ON-DISABLE: resolve `1b` to the FIRST definition instead of the nearest and `loop_twice` returns a wrong value (exit 12); drop `templateTextForms` from a dialect and its forms are refused by name. Exit codes 11–17 name the shape that went wrong.
